notes.statement: The opening source sentence includes “on reste en plan”, then introduces the four-element set C in display (17). The word plan is visibly legible. The two cap-shaped superscripts in that display are retained with top first and plus as the recurring alternate.

Display (22) writes \varepsilon_1^+<\varepsilon_2^- and \varepsilon_2^+<\varepsilon_1^-. The following diagram has four black points and arrows from the lower points to the opposite upper points. One diagonal is interrupted at the crossing, and a cancelled \varepsilon_2^+ remains beneath the lower-left point.

Section 1.3 begins with a cancelled family description, then display (23). The body revises famille with the interlinear ens. (...) group. The adjective indiciellement is read from the surviving loops and turns; the short preceding word remains noté/écrit/écrite. The margin writes a nested P expression with a closing parenthesis immediately after the innermost capital, before (X).

The source’s display (24) uses the written abbreviation mut with raised t and a point, followed by non panachées. The added heading Déf introduces the source’s naming of the family as non panachée, followed by terminology for strictement non panachée. The slanted marginal naming phrase includes Card A=n/nu and the underlined words décomposition and n-aire.

Display (25) writes C as the coproduct of the omega_alpha. The right-hand interlinear addition mentions the written ss p^t fixe involution sigma and a transposition on each omega_alpha. A cancelled word beneath transposition remains unreadable. The main text resumes with the order relation and ends at the bottom with a.

The sheet has section number 1.3 and display labels (17), (22), (23), (24), (25). The pencil 37 at the lower left is retained as an archive-sheet comment. No separate author page number, written date or independent title is visible. No explicit source proof-check or question mark appears.

Same-page mathematical notation supplied local shape comparisons: the epsilon turns recur in the displays and diagram, omega recurs in (17), (23) and (25), and the capital Pi caps/legs recur throughout. The clearly crossed diagram plus signs were compared with the short cap-and-downstem signs in (17). These were handwriting comparisons; no proof, re-proof or computation was performed.

H’s explicit notes were read: it identifies the four diagram elements as points and acknowledges the lower-left cancellation; it identifies two oblique margin notes in the author’s hand; and it identifies the involution passage as an interlinear addition to the right of (25), with the page ending on a. These declarations were considered when collating state and notation. Its claim about a title on page 31 was not investigated, because this reading is restricted to scan038.
